hypothesis: The parent's query budget slack is eaten by (a) a known zero-information query being sent when all retries fail (i171: four retries ping-ponged between rejected A(1,1,1)/B(1,1,1), then the first rejected pick B(1,1,1) was sent) and (b) accepting any informative split, so the model often takes 1-vs-3 or 0.65-bit splits while 1.0-bit splits are on offer (i284 ended at 17/18 queries, i266 at 16/18). Offering and accepting only the most even splits, never sending a zero-info query, and listing already-rejected picks in the retry message will keep every episode at 100% end-of-episode uniqueness with fewer queries (mean below the parent's 12.9) and zero zero-information queries.
behavior_changes: Query menu lists only the splits tied for the most even split (max marginal entropy), titled 'Best queries now ... pick one of these'; weaker splits are no longer shown.
A reply is accepted on the first pass only if it names one of those best splits.
An informative but uneven pick is rejected with feedback 'only splits the candidates n1 vs n0' and kept as a last-resort fallback after MAX_TRIES (still the model's own query).

Zero-information, repeated or solved-circuit picks are never used as the fallback: if no informative pick appears in MAX_TRIES, nothing is sent and the turn is re-asked (solve() already handles None without spending budget).
Retry messages append 'Already rejected this turn: ...' with every rejected query so the model stops alternating between the same rejected picks.
preserved_behaviors: Rules-derived enumeration of the hypothesis space (two 2-input gates + NOTs per circuit, inventory split without replacement) and the relaxed fallback.
Compact state text: answers, SOLVED circuits with 'Do NOT query again', candidate lists when <= 8.
Querying stops as soon as every circuit has a single candidate.
Final step unchanged: numbered candidates, 'A: n, B: n, C: n' picks, assembled 24-bit guess.
The model writes every query; the harness only vetoes and re-asks.
verification: Replayed the parent's 10 trace histories through its own candidate space: i171 query 7 B(1,1,1) was zero-information (sent via fallback after 4 rejected retries); many accepted queries were well below the best available split (e.g. 0.65/1.00, 0.72/1.00 in i238/i284/i266).

Offline simulation on the rules' own space (150 random consistent truths per batch inventory, no labels): accepting any split exceeds 18 queries in ~1-3% of truths for most inventories; accepting only best splits brings worst case to 16-17 for {AND3,OR3,NOT1}.
Ran check_b2r0_cand_pilot_strict_b10g3r2_b2r0g0.py: 10/10 status=ok, 10/10 parsed_final_guess, 0 crashes, queries_used = 12,11,12,17,6,13,13,13,13,5 (mean 11.5 vs parent 12.9).
Replayed the new histories: every accepted query was a best split (h == hmax), zero zero-information queries, all 10 episodes end with exactly one candidate for each of A, B, C, no relaxed fallback.

Final step: the model answered 'A: 1, B: 1, C: 1' in all 10 and the returned guess equals the three SOLVED tables. Re-asks: only 6 single retries (first-turn A(0,0,0) 20 vs 32), fixed in one retry; the weak-pick fallback was never needed.
risks: Greedy best-marginal-split is not joint-optimal: i0 (inventory AND1/OR5/NOT2) still needed 17/18 queries with every query a best split; simulation shows ~2% of truths for that inventory can exceed 18 even under greedy.

Showing only best splits narrows the menu; if the model keeps picking off-menu, extra LLM calls are spent (bounded by MAX_TRIES per turn and wasted < budget turns), and repeated total failure could end querying early.

Correctness still relies on the harness's reading of the rules (no fan-out, signals consumed); if the real generator differs, 'SOLVED' could be wrong; the relaxed fallback only triggers on outright contradiction.
